READ_THIS_FIRST: Kosher alcohol data from the official STAR-K and cRc listings. Six categories.
SAFETY RULE 1: lists containing '4' = the agency says NOT APPROVED / NOT RECOMMENDED. Never present such a product as kosher or approved.
SAFETY RULE 2: the agencies are SEPARATE and sometimes differ. Report each ruling on its own.
SAFETY RULE 3: lists OVERLAP. Never add list totals.
SAFETY RULE 4: absence from this file means NOTHING. Say you have no data.

SAFETY RULE 5: LIST 1 MEANS 'APPROVED ONLY WHEN BEARING THE REQUIRED KOSHER SYMBOL'. It is the agency's CONDITION OF APPROVAL. It is NOT a claim that any bottle was physically observed carrying the mark.

SAFETY RULE 6: NO record in this dataset reports physical observation of a label. Never say a bottle 'is confirmed to carry' a symbol. Say the agency REQUIRES the symbol for approval, so the buyer must check.
SAFETY RULE 7: symbol_required '?' means the agency is SILENT. Silence is NOT 'no symbol required'.
SAFETY RULE 8: '-P' marks (OU-P, OK-P, Star-K-P) are Passover certifications, DIFFERENT from the plain symbol.
SAFETY RULE 9: the Liqueur category is LIMITED SCOPE - certified bottles only, not comparable to the other five.
SAFETY RULE 10: absence from the Liqueur category means NOTHING. Liqueur holds only certified bottles; not-approved liqueurs were deliberately excluded. Never read Liqueur absence as 'not approved'.
